answer: Cross-Challenge Response Vault. Each identity must answer a fresh challenge derived from a secret it holds in a vault and from a rotating public seed, then submit the response through a separate ferrous token ring that only accepts one solution per seed. A wrong or reused answer locks the ring and forfeits the account’s umber reserve, a fixed per-attempt charge. To farm N identities an attacker must provision N distinct secrets up front and pay the reserve N times, so mass registration costs scale linearly with accounts while single-use responses stay unrepeatable.
